family: FAMILY IS ONE SOUND LOOSE THING TAKEN IN HAND, LOOKED AT, AND PUT DOWN AGAIN. Nothing lifted off the ground, nothing unfastened, unfilled, unscrewed, unpegged or turned out of its holder, and the thing goes back the way it came. NO CUSTOMER TOLD, REFUSED OR PASSED. THE SECOND PERSON IS SHOWN AND NEVER REPORTED AND MAY NOT TOUCH THE THING IN HAND, WHICH IS IN THE BAND PERSON'S HAND FOR MOST OF THE CHAPTER. THE AMENDMENT THE REVIEW OF 0066 MADE TO THE 0066 RULE IS IN FORCE AND ONE WORD IS CUT OUT OF IT: ASKED. THE SECOND PERSON MAY BE ASKED A PLAIN QUESTION AND MAY ANSWER IT, AND MAY SAY ONE THING THAT IS NOT ABOUT THE JOB, AND THE PERSON DOING THE WORK MAY ANSWER THAT BACK. WHAT MAY NOT HAPPEN IS THAT ANYBODY IS TOLD ANYTHING ABOUT THE WORK, REFUSES ANYTHING, OR PASSES THE WORK ON.
why_not_the_nearest: 0065 was one sound shallow fix on tired ground with a tool. 0066 was one sound shallow keep on ground already moved with a tool. HERE THE TOOL IS GONE AND THE WHOLE OF THE LOOKING IS DONE WITH THE HANDS.
family_nearest_turned_away_from: No material is moved from one place to another. No joint is filled, no channel is opened, no guide is brushed, no rail is combed, no face is swept, no tray is emptied and no drawer is eased. All ten jobs end with the object where it was.
ten_gestures_and_the_rule_about_them: THE GESTURE IS THE ACTION OF THE HAND AND NOT THE OBJECT, AND NO TWO CHAPTERS MAY USE THE SAME GESTURE. TEN DIFFERENT HANDS. TURNED OVER IN THE HAND AND PUT BACK IS ONE GESTURE AND IS NOT USED IN ANY OF THE TEN. THIS IS THE FAULT THE REVIEW OF 0066 FOUND IN FOUR OF THE TEN CARDS AS FIRST ISSUED, AT 0855, 0858, 0859 AND 0861, AND THE FOUR CARDS BELOW CARRY FOUR DIFFERENT HANDS, WHICH WAS CONFIRMED BEFORE ANY PROSE.

bands.figure_rule_for_this_block: Five standing figures, one band each, kept for the whole block, and no figure anywhere in the ten is aged except those five. The late fifties stays at number nine alone, two chapters, 0855 and 0864. No new early or late fifties. The new unaged ceiling of four is not used: every one of the ten arrivals is a figure already on the page.

figure_rule_for_the_block_on_arithmetic: Single-place counts only, and a figure the chapter sets must close. No arithmetic engine: no spread, no telephone, no sum worked out to reveal something, no number asked to agree with a number in another chapter. Every count made in one place and kept by the ending. The figures in this block are: three holes in one gate post, of which two have taken a wedge; two wedges at one gate, one in the post and one on the flag; one trowel with an inch of it blunt; one nut and one quarter turn; one worm and one card; one lump and one arm's length; one stone off a heap of about six feet; one sheet and one nail; one hinge and one quarter inch; one thread and three inches; one mushroom and one hole.

cards.0855: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has two iron wedges at the gate, one driven into the post and one lying loose on the flag it came off, and means to weigh the loose one in the palm and put it back down on the same flag with the same face up; the stop is where the palm can tell that the weight in it moves across the palm and does not stay put.
cards.0856: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has the front inch of her own trowel gone blunt and means to turn it in the hand and read it on a stone of the edging heap and put it back on its nail; the stop is where the edge skates across a face instead of biting into it.
cards.0857: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has the front wheel nut of the barrow turned a quarter off the flats and means to bring it back onto the flats with her fingers and put it back, and the spanner is not picked up and nothing else touches the nut; the stop is where the nut bites on the corner of a flat and stops turning.
cards.0858: At the unit a man in his early forties has an earthworm out on the flags in the yard and means to lift it on the flat of a card and set it down on the same flag a foot clear of the trodden line without carrying it off the flags; the stop is where the worm moves on the card and not on the hand.
cards.0859: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has the spoil heap of the broken apron base at her feet and means to take a lump off it, hold it out at arm's length and look at it edge-on to see what is stuck to it, and put it back without picking anything off it; the stop is where the mortar shows along the edge and not on the face.
cards.0860: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has six feet of edging in a heap at the gate and means to take one stone off it, rub along its top face with a thumb and read it for the tooling, and put it back where it came off without picking the grit out of its hollows; the stop is where the thumb finds the lines under the grit.
cards.0861: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a bent nail loose in the yard and a pile of old nails by the gate, and means to shake the bent one once by the head over a sheet so the loose rust comes off it and put it down by the gate where nails go; the stop is where the rust comes off as dust and the metal under it is whole.
cards.0862: At the unit a man in his early forties has the top hinge of the near gate with play in it and means to lift the top of the gate a quarter inch by hand and let it back down; the stop is where the gate comes down on the pin and the latch still catches.
cards.0863: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a loose thread off the mouth of the hessian sack and means to draw it out between two fingers and put it down again; the stop is where the thread comes away whole for about three inches and stops.
cards.0864: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a small mushroom out of the side of the turf stack and means to take it off in the hand and put it down on the grass; the stop is where it comes away whole in one movement instead of leaving its foot in the face of the stack.

datelines.0858: Saturday the fourth of November 2023, on the flags in the yard at the unit from the time the frost has gone off them until the light has gone off the wall. There is a worm on them.
datelines.0859: Tuesday the seventh of November 2023, in the yard at the lock-up from first light until the office glass has gone dark, and the lump of the broken base read edge-on is the whole of that Tuesday.
datelines.0860: Monday the thirteenth of November 2023, at the heap by the gate at number twelve from the time the shadow has come off it until the light has gone. One stone, and a thumb across the top of it.
datelines.0861: Thursday the sixteenth of November 2023, at the gate end of the yard at the lock-up from the time the dew has come off the steel until the last of the light goes. Nails, and a sheet, and about two minutes.
datelines.0862: Sunday the nineteenth of November 2023, at the near gate of the unit yard from the time the frost has gone to the first of the hand, and the quarter inch the hinge gives is the whole of that Sunday.
datelines.0863: Friday the twenty-fourth of November 2023, in that shed at number ten from the time the door has gone light until the middle of the afternoon. A thread, and the length of it.
datelines.0864: Monday the twenty-seventh of November 2023, at the turf stack at number nine from the time the frost has gone off the top of it until the street has gone quiet. A mushroom, and the hole it came out of.

declared_ordinary_word_note: DECLARED BEFORE ANY PROSE OF 855 TO 864 EXISTS. IT IS NOT DUST, WHICH WAS 0065, IT IS NOT EDGE, WHICH WAS 0066, AND IT IS NOT ANY WORD ON THE OLD LIST. IT MAY NOT BE not, usually, anyway, like, just, enough, still, kind, quite, small, round, one, week, almost, anything, and then, nearly, away, count, garden, shoulder, work. GRAIN IS THE ORDINARY WORD OF THIS BLOCK AND IT IS USED FOR THE DIRECTION A MATERIAL RUNS IN: THE GRAIN OF TIMBER, THE GRAIN OF STONE, THE GRAIN OF A HESSIAN WEAVE, THE GRAIN OF A SOIL FACE, THE GRAIN OF RUST. IT IS AN ORDINARY WORD AND NOT A FIGURE.
anti_tick_rules_written_before_any_prose: NO CHAPTER ENDS ON A JOB FINISHED AND NONE ENDS ON THE THING BEING PUT BACK. FOUR END ON A THING LEFT AS IT IS AND NOT PUT THERE BY THIS WORK: 0855 THE THIRD HOLE IN THE GATE POST, 0859 THE MORTAR ON THE LUMPS OF THE BASE, 0861 THE WIRE NAILS LEFT IN THE PILE, 0864 THE HOLE IN THE SIDE OF THE TURF STACK.

THE SECOND PERSON IS SHOWN AND NEVER REPORTED, EXCEPT WHERE THE REVIEW OF 0066 CUT ONE WORD OUT OF THE RULE. NOBODY IS TOLD ANYTHING ABOUT THE WORK, NOBODY REFUSES ANYTHING, NOBODY IS PASSED THE WORK, NOTHING PASSES BETWEEN PEOPLE ABOUT THE JOB, NOBODY HOLDS ANYTHING OF OURS AND NOBODY LOOKS TWICE. A PLAIN QUESTION MAY BE ASKED AND ANSWERED AND ONE THING THAT IS NOT ABOUT THE JOB MAY BE SAID AND ANSWERED BACK.
A FIGURE THE CHAPTER ITSELF SETS MUST CLOSE. WHERE A COUNT IS MADE IT IS MADE ONCE AND THE ENDING KEEPS IT. SINGLE-PLACE COUNTS ONLY.
THE TEN GESTURES ARE THE ACTION OF THE HAND AND NOT THE OBJECT, AND NO TWO OF THEM ARE THE SAME, AND THE OBJECT IS NOT WHAT VARIES THE CHAPTER.
THE TEN DATELINES ARE TEN DIFFERENT CONSTRUCTIONS AND THE CLOSER AND THE TASK IS THE WHOLE OF THAT WEEKDAY IS IN TWO OF THEM ONLY.
NO WATER IS DRAWN, CARRIED, POURED OR EMPTIED BY ANYBODY AT WORK IN ANY OF THE TEN. THE ONLY WATER IN THE TEN IS RAIN AND THE WEATHER.
NO CEMENT, MORTAR OR NEW CONCRETE IS PUT DOWN ANYWHERE IN THE TEN. THE MORTAR ON THE LUMPS IN 0859 IS MORTAR THAT WAS ALREADY ON THEM.
still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: THE EIGHT SPENT THINGS MAY NOT BE SPENT AGAIN: no moss in a joint, no tuft of grass in a kerb joint, no band of pale plaster behind a rail, no chipped arris left bare, no old grease across the foot of a guide, no bright patch on a corner, no worn place on a rail, no joint left unfed because the thing above it is proud. NONE OF THE EIGHT APPEARS IN ANY OF THE TEN. THE THREE BLINDING JOBS MAY NOT BE RUN AS ONE JOB: 0845 fine dust on a level run, 0849 coarse at the bottom and fine on top, 0853 grit on a fall. NONE OF THE TEN IS A BLINDING JOB AT ALL, BECAUSE NOTHING IN THE TEN IS LAID OR PACKED.
